about: Monthly home checks used by My Home and the seasonal alert email. 'months' are 1-12. 'when' narrows an item to matching homes: an item applies when ANY of its heating/cooling/water_supply lists matches the home (values from the Home Energy Planner; an unknown heating or cooling counts as a match, an unknown water supply does not). 'noAudit' skips homes with that test on record within 'years'. Every item names its source.

items.title: Book the yearly inspection of your fuel-burning heating
items.body: Health Canada says to have fuel-burning appliances inspected by a professional every year. Book it before the first cold snap, when technicians fill up.

items.title: Check the furnace filter
items.body: NRCan suggests changing or cleaning the filter on a forced-air system about every 3 months, or sooner if it looks loaded.

items.title: If you have an HRV or ERV, clean its filters
items.body: NRCan's guidance is to clean HRV and ERV filters every 1 to 3 months so the unit keeps moving fresh air.

items.title: Test your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms
items.body: When the clocks change, press the test button on every smoke and carbon monoxide alarm, and replace any unit past the date printed on it.

items.title: Start a long-term radon test
items.body: Health Canada says to test for at least 3 months, mostly during the heating season, on the lowest level you spend time in. A lab kit costs about $30 to $80.

items.title: Test your well water after the spring thaw
items.body: Spring, after snowmelt, is when most provinces suggest testing a private well for bacteria. Your provincial guidance is below.

items.title: Test your well water again this fall
items.body: Fall rains can carry bacteria into wells. Ontario health units suggest testing in spring, summer and fall; Quebec and New Brunswick suggest spring and fall.

items.title: Seal the easy air leaks before winter
items.body: NRCan says about a quarter of a typical home's heat loss can be air leakage. Weatherstrip doors and attic hatches and caulk around trim before it gets cold.

items.title: Set the thermostat back at night
items.body: NRCan estimates about 2% of heating energy saved for each degree you turn it down for 8 hours. NRCan suggests 17 °C asleep or away and 20 °C when you're home.

items.title: Keep winter humidity low enough to keep windows dry
items.body: CMHC says to keep indoor humidity near 30% when it's below −10 °C outside (as low as 25% in extreme cold). Health Canada's range for the rest of the year is 30% to 50%.

items.title: Get the air conditioner or heat pump ready for summer
items.body: Clean or replace the filter and clear leaves and debris from the outdoor unit. Hydro-Québec says a poorly maintained heat pump can use up to 25% more electricity.
